conventions.convention: A semigroup family satisfies Φ₀ = id and Φₜ₊ₛ = Φₜ ∘ Φₛ. CP-divisibility requires a CPTP factor Vₜ,ₛ for every 0 ≤ s ≤ t; neither definition imposes continuity or claims a universal definition of Markovianity.
The system is the first tensor factor. The initial assignment is ρ ⊗ η with η fixed independently of ρ. Joint unitaries satisfy U₀ = I but need not be continuous or obey a group law.

Finite unitary reduction and the time-homogeneous GKSL approximation are separate model choices. Time is in seconds, H in joules, ℏ in joule-seconds, and jump matrices in seconds to the power −1/2. No microscopic reservoir limit or empirical observation is asserted.

Ordered-simplex integrals are nested coordinatewise Riemann integrals, integrating the earliest time first. Equal-endpoint integrals are zero; the zero-variable integral is evaluation, with volume factor 1 even at T = 0.

A branch operator places later jumps to the left, with no-jump propagators between consecutive jumps. Its trace weight is a density in the jump times, with units seconds to the power −n. An empty jump family has no positive-jump branches.
Amplitude damping uses the ordered basis (|0⟩, |1⟩), H = ℏω|1⟩⟨1| and L = √γ|0⟩⟨1|, with real ω and γ ≥ 0. Consequently the 01 coherence has phase +iωt.

load_bearing.statement: For finite system and environment spaces, adopt the fixed product preparation ρ ⊗ η and reduced evolution Tr_E(Uₜ(ρ ⊗ η)Uₜ*). A time-homogeneous finite GKSL model may instead be selected as a separate approximation; selecting it is not a consequence of finite unitary reduction.

Continuous finite-dimensional integrands on the closed ordered simplex have recursively defined coordinate integrals; every partial integral is continuous in its remaining parameters. Integration is linear, basis-independent, commutes with finite-dimensional linear maps, preserves scalar nonnegativity, and satisfies ‖Iₙ(F)‖ ≤ C Tⁿ/n! when ‖F‖ ≤ C, with the stated zero-variable and zero-time conventions.

For finite GKSL data, define K = −iH/ℏ − ΣₐLₐ*Lₐ/2 and R(u) = exp(uK). Define each ordered jump branch by alternating no-jump propagators and its specified jump matrices, its branch state by WρW*, and its weight density by Tr(WρW*). This definition alone does not assert normalization.

For the selected finite time-homogeneous GKSL model, each R(u) is a contraction, branch states are positive for positive inputs, and exp(tℒ)(ρ) equals the sum of all ordered jump-branch integrals for every density matrix ρ and t ≥ 0. The series converges in trace norm uniformly on bounded time intervals, and all branch weights sum to one.
In the finite product-state model, Φₜ(X) = Tr_E(Uₜ(X ⊗ η)Uₜ*) is a finite quantum channel for each t ≥ 0. The family need not obey the semigroup law and need not be CP-divisible.
For H = ℏω|1⟩⟨1| and L = √γ|0⟩⟨1| with γ ≥ 0, the GKSL solution has ρ₁₁(t) = exp(−γt)ρ₁₁(0), ρ₀₀(t) = ρ₀₀(0) + (1 − exp(−γt))ρ₁₁(0), and coherence factors exp((±iω − γ/2)t).

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite Hermitian spectral decomposition, positive matrices, density matrices and trace calculus.
Exact definitions of complete positivity, trace preservation and finite quantum channels.
Finite GKSL generator, commutator and anticommutator conventions, and physical units.
Kraus-form complete positivity and the adjoint-square criterion for trace preservation.
CPTP and semigroup properties of the finite GKSL exponential, including trace preservation used to normalize branch weights.
System-first tensor order and the coordinate contraction defining the environment partial trace.
Changing to an environment eigenbasis without changing the reduced map.
Completeness of finite matrix and superoperator spaces.
Trace-norm bounds for left and right multiplication and continuity of trace.
Operator exponential convergence, differentiation, exponential law and norm bounds.
The induced trace-norm superoperator norm in the jump-expansion estimates.
Underlying scalar integral used in the coordinatewise simplex construction.
Equal-endpoint integrals and degenerate simplex conventions.
Integrability of continuous coordinate functions and derivative components on nondegenerate compact intervals.
Coordinate changes, finite sums and commutation with finite-dimensional linear maps.
Nonnegativity and scalar bounds for recursive integrals.
Tagged-sum convergence used to prove the vector-valued integral norm inequality.
Affine substitution to a fixed unit interval when proving continuity of partial integrals.
Compactness of the closed bounded parameter domains.
Uniform continuity needed for parameter continuity of partial integrals.
Monomial integral evaluations, the no-jump contraction argument and entrywise variation of constants.
Monomial primitives and the ordered-simplex volume Tⁿ/n!.
Scalar power-series evaluation of the two-qubit unitary and damping coefficients.
Complex phase multiplication and identification with the real exponential.
Unit-modulus phases and the cosine coherence multiplier in the recurrence model.
Existence of a positive phase giving zero coherence and subsequent sign-reversed revival.
The zero-survival limit establishing total mass one for the positive-rate first-jump density.
